supportedFacts: AI includes symbolic, neural, evolutionary, and multi-agent approaches.
Machine learning uses data to learn task behaviour; narrow task success is not general competence.

supportedFacts: Knowledge representation includes graphs, logic, rules and structured relations.
Expert systems combine a knowledge base and inference; rule conditions can be traced against facts.

supportedFacts: A perceptron combines input features using weights and a threshold for binary classification.
Training seeks weight values that reduce classification errors.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: A loss measures discrepancy between predictions and expected outputs.
Gradient methods adjust parameters; multilayer networks use nonlinear transformations and backpropagation computes derivatives.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Frameworks support tensor operations and automatic differentiation.
Overfitting can produce low training error and higher validation error; complexity, data and regularisation affect it.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Images have grid/tensor representations and convolution applies shared local filters across positions.
Networks can learn filters and combine local visual patterns through layers.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Pretrained visual models can serve as feature extractors for another task.
Adaptation requires relevant new labels and evaluation; reuse is not a guarantee of target-task success.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Object detection predicts categories and locations, often bounding boxes.
Detection quality involves location/overlap and class-specific errors, rather than image classification alone.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Segmentation classifies pixels or regions for more precise localisation.
Semantic and instance segmentation distinguish class masks and object instances.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Text tokenisation can use characters, words or subwords mapped into numerical representations.
Bag-of-words drops order; TF-IDF weights terms by within-document frequency and collection prevalence.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Embeddings represent tokens using dense numerical vectors.
Learned semantic representations reflect distributional patterns; relationships in representation are not guaranteed synonymy.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Attention weights contextual relationships between sequence positions.
Transformers combine attention with position information; context affects representations.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Language models support text prediction/generation from context.
Prompts specify tasks and examples can illustrate task patterns; generation is not source verification.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Genetic search uses candidate representations, a fitness objective, selection, crossover and mutation.
Constraints and valid candidate representations matter; search can find local rather than guaranteed global optima.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Reinforcement learning relates states/observations, actions, environment transitions, rewards and a policy.
Policy learning seeks reward over interaction; the chosen reward defines incentives.
sources.reviewScope: Teaching chapter reviewed; original fictional exercises and assessment items authored separately.

supportedFacts: Multiple interacting agents can create collective behaviour using local rules.
Reactive and deliberative agents use different decision structures; interactions affect results.

supportedFacts: Responsible AI principles include fairness, reliability/safety, privacy/security, inclusion, transparency and accountability.
